why: Both records are child records, both Family IDs are known and checksum-valid, they DIFFER, and the creation types are the same: the pair must REJECT. This rule is why the Family ID exists (operator, 2026-09-16). Two series each have an episode called 'Pilot' in the same year -- the single most reused episode title there is -- and before compare-spec 2.11.0 this exact shape was held at Review twice over: the cross-type review floor's title-strong trigger accepted the bare exact title as corroboration, and where an alt-id CONFLICT existed, the alt-penalty floor computed its precondition from the UNGATED confidence and restored a score the gate had already ruled out. Found live in the Tamr audit: a 'Pilot' held at Review against candidates from five different families. Fixed by scoping the title trigger to pairs with a non-child side and gating the penalty floor on eligibility; this pair pins the combined outcome.
